title: Sara's options
primary_topics: SC en banc resolution in Torreon v. House committee on justice (Aug. 5, 2026) dismissing petitions against the VP's impeachment on mootness -- possibly a signal the Court will not be dragged into partisan dramas absent grave abuse of discretion
Three complementary options for VP Sara: defend herself to the end, resign, and/or rally public support

Option 1: defense -- challenges to admissibility and relevance; open questions on whether she will testify, her demeanor, cross-examination, and how she will explain alleged threats to the First Family, confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bank deposits and tax records

Option 2: resignation -- removal moot, but the Senate may continue by majority and impose perpetual disqualification by two-thirds, barring a 2028 presidential run; Corona (2012) disqualified vs Sereno (quo warranto) not; Nixon's one-sentence 1974 resignation

Option 3: rally public support like Bill Clinton, acquitted in 1999 with approval ratings above 60 percent; impeachment is tried before a political body where public sentiment is often decisive; possible effect of former President Duterte's return 'dead or alive'
Closing -- impeachment preserves the integrity of governance and 'a public office is a public trust'; the Constitution must endure as the citadel of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law

stances.claim: VP Sara has at least three complementary options: defend herself to the end, resign, and/or rally public support to avert conviction.

If she resigns, removal becomes moot, but the Senate may continue by majority and impose perpetual disqualification by two-thirds, which would bar her 2028 run, as Corona was disqualified while Sereno was not.
Like Clinton, who was acquitted with approval ratings above 60 percent, she may rally public support, since impeachment is tried before a political body where public sentiment often decides.
Former President Duterte's return, dead or alive, could change the political dynamic, though whether that pivot would apply remains uncertain.
Whatever her choice, impeachment preserves the integrity of governance, and the Constitution must endure as the ultimate compass under the rule of law.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban calls the Supreme Court's Aug. 5, 2026 resolution in Torreon v. House committee on justice, dismissing the petitions against VP Sara Duterte's impeachment on mootness, a turning point that may signal the Court will not be dragged into partisan dramas unless the impeachment court commits grave abuse of discretion. He then outlines three complementary options for the VP. First, defend herself to the end: her team challenges the admissibility of evidence and the relevance of allegations, and CJP asks whether she will testify, whether she will be aggressive (as with a sheriff serving a court order) or measured, who would cross-examine her, and how she will explain alleged threats to the First Family, confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bank deposits and tax records. Second, resign: removal would become moot, but the senator-judges could continue the trial by majority vote and, by two-thirds, impose perpetual disqualification, barring her 2028 presidential run. Corona was removed and disqualified in 2012, while Sereno, ousted by an 8-6 quo warranto ruling, was not disqualified; Nixon resigned in 1974 with a one-sentence letter after losing the people's trust. Third, rally public support, as Bill Clinton did, remaining above 60 percent approval and winning acquittal in 1999; impeachment is tried before a political body where public sentiment often decides. The dynamic could shift if former President Rodrigo R. Duterte returns from detention in The Hague, dead or alive. CJP concludes that the trial transcends the fortunes of officials: impeachment preserves the integrity of governance and the principle that a public office is a public trust, and whatever happens, the Constitution must endure as the citadel of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law.
